hypothesis: The selected lead-directed decoder was valid but measured slower than baseline, while predicate aggregation was valid and near baseline speed; neither result establishes the cause. This pure-scalar variant tests whether deriving the continuation count from lead comparisons and sharing a continuation loop reduces the width-specific control flow. The extra loop and boundary checks may instead cost more, so controller measurement is needed.
notes: Pure-scalar candidate; no performance claim is made before controller measurement. A prior compact-DFA development variant (e87168de8c614fc4-h01) failed protected correctness checks; the available record does not identify why. This proposal uses a shared continuation loop instead of reusing that DFA.
transformations: Retain the ASCII-run fast path and the existing ABI and output behavior.
Replace separate width-specific continuation validation with a continuation count derived from lead-byte comparisons and a shared loop.
Check the remaining length before continuation loads and preserve the E0, ED, F0, and F4 second-byte restrictions.
